facts.statement: If both boxers are in their corners, Jab does nothing because you cannot reach your opponent.
facts.sourceSentence: If both boxers are in their corners: Do nothing. You can't reach your opponent!

facts.statement: If not both in their corners, Jab flips one of the opponent's Guard cards from ready to exhausted.
facts.sourceSentence: If not: Flip one of your opponent's Guard cards from ready to exhausted.

facts.statement: If all of the opponent's Guard cards are already exhausted, Jab does nothing.
facts.sourceSentence: If all their Guard cards are already exhausted, do nothing.

facts.statement: Jab cannot break a Guard card.
facts.sourceSentence: A Jab cannot break a Guard card (see Punch).

facts.statement: If already in your corner, Retreat does nothing.
facts.sourceSentence: If you are already in your corner: Do nothing. You're already against the ropes!

facts.statement: If in the center ring, Retreat moves your boxer to your corner.
facts.sourceSentence: If you are in the center ring: Move your boxer to your corner.

facts.statement: If already in the center ring or your opponent also plays Advance for the same action, Advance does nothing.
facts.sourceSentence: If you are already in the center ring and/or your opponent also plays an Advance card for the same action: Do nothing. You're just butting heads!

facts.statement: If conditions are not met, Advance moves your boxer to the center ring.
facts.sourceSentence: If not: Move your boxer to the center ring.

facts.statement: When you Advance to the center ring, if your opponent is in the center ring, they are pushed into their corner.
facts.sourceSentence: If your opponent is in the center ring, also push them into their corner.

facts.statement: If opponent plays Punch for the same action, Block ignores any effect the Punch has on you.
facts.sourceSentence: If your opponent plays a Punch card for the same action: Ignore any effect their Punch has on you (see Punch).

facts.statement: Block actions do not block Jabs.
facts.sourceSentence: Block actions do not block Jabs.

facts.statement: If opponent does not play Punch for the same action, Block does nothing.
facts.sourceSentence: If not: Do nothing.

facts.statement: If in your corner, Punch requires you to flip one Guard card from ready to exhausted before resolving the Punch.
facts.sourceSentence: If you are in your corner: Flip one of your Guard cards from ready to exhausted, then resolve your Punch.

facts.statement: If in your corner with no ready Guard cards, Punch does nothing.
facts.sourceSentence: If you do not have any ready Guard cards, do nothing. You're up against the ropes!

facts.statement: If in the center ring, Punch is resolved without flipping your own Guard card.
facts.sourceSentence: If you are in the center ring: Resolve your Punch without flipping your Guard card. You've got 'em on the ropes!

facts.statement: If your Punch is blocked or both you and your opponent are in your respective corners, your Punch has no effect on your opponent.
facts.sourceSentence: If your Punch is blocked (see Block) or both you and your opponent are in your respective corners: Your Punch has no effect on your opponent...

facts.statement: Even if your Punch has no effect, you must still exhaust your own Guard card if you are in your corner.
facts.sourceSentence: ...however, you must still exhaust your own guard card if you are in your corner.

facts.statement: If your Punch is not blocked and your opponent has at least one exhausted Guard card, one of their exhausted Guard cards is broken and removed from the game.
facts.sourceSentence: If your Punch is not blocked and your opponent has at least one exhausted Guard card: Break one of your opponent's exhausted Guard cards by removing it from the game and returning it to the box.

facts.statement: If your Punch is not blocked and your opponent has no exhausted Guard cards, one of the opponent's Guard cards is flipped from ready to exhausted instead.
facts.sourceSentence: If your Punch is not blocked and your opponent does not have any exhausted Guard cards: Instead of breaking their Guard, flip one of your opponent's Guard cards from ready to exhausted.

facts.statement: If both you and your opponent play Punch for the same action while one player is in the center ring, the player punching from their corner must finish exhausting their Guard card before either player resolves their Punch.
facts.sourceSentence: If both you and your opponent play a Punch for the same action while one player is in the center ring: The player punching from their corner must finish exhausting their Guard card (if able) before either player may resolve their Punch.

facts.statement: When resting, you reclaim all action cards from your discard pile and add them to your hand.
facts.sourceSentence: Reclaim your discards: Take all the action cards in your discard pile and add them to your hand.

facts.statement: When resting, do not take any action cards currently in play.
facts.sourceSentence: Do not take any of the action cards currently in play.

facts.statement: If any of your Guard cards are exhausted, Rest allows you to flip one Guard card back to ready.
facts.sourceSentence: If any of your Guard cards are EXHAUSTED: Flip one Guard card back to ready.

facts.statement: Flipping a Guard card back to ready when resting happens in addition to reclaiming discards.
facts.sourceSentence: This is in addition to reclaiming your discards.

facts.statement: The first set of action cards must be completely compared and resolved before the second set of action cards are flipped face up.
facts.sourceSentence: When you are done comparing and resolving the first action cards, DO NOT discard them yet. Leave them in place and flip the second action cards face up. Then, compare and resolve the second action cards just like you did with the first action cards.

facts.statement: After comparing and resolving both sets of action cards, place the two action cards played that round into the discard pile and begin a new round.
facts.sourceSentence: After you have compared and resolved both the first and second sets of action cards, place your two action cards played this round into your discard pile, and then begin a new round.

facts.statement: Do not discard any cards until the discard phase.
facts.sourceSentence: DO NOT DISCARD ANY CARDS UNTIL THIS PHASE.

facts.statement: Breaking all of the opponent's Guard cards results in a knockout and an immediate win.
facts.sourceSentence: Once a player has broken all 3 of their opponent's Guard cards, they have knocked them out and immediately win the game!

facts.statement: If both players knock each other out during the same action, the game is a draw.
facts.sourceSentence: If both players manage to knock each other out during the same action, it is a draw.

facts.statement: In the plan phase, you may place any action cards in any order regardless of their timings.
facts.sourceSentence: In the plan phase, you may place any action cards, regardless of their timings, in any order. The timing on the cards does not matter in this phase.

facts.statement: In the fight phase, the first set of action cards is always completely resolved before the second set of action cards, so effects from the first set do not carry over to the second set.
facts.sourceSentence: In the fight phase, the first set of action cards are always completely resolved before the second set of action cards. For example, a Block from the first action will not stop a Punch from the second action.
